newsitem.title: KENYA: Tourists sunbathe as violence engulfs Kenya resort.
newsitem.headline: Tourists sunbathe as violence engulfs Kenya resort.

text.p: Tour operators appear more nervous about the violence swirling around the Kenyan port of Mombasa than the tourists sunning themselves nearby on the golden sands of the Indian Ocean beaches.

At least 31 people have been killed in villages around Mombasa in five days as gangs armed with machetes and automatic rifles have terrorised the local population, prompting the government to send in the armed forces in a massive security operation.
But, apart from seeing soldiers and police combing the area, most tourists at Diani, 30 km (20 miles) south of Mombasa, remained blissfully ignorant of the chaos.
"We have heard rumours about violence but we are not affected at all. We have taken a tour to the park and now we have returned to the beach," said Swiss tourist Peter Kunz.
"The general feeling is that no one is harassing us," he added, echoing the sentiments of many of the foreign visitors.
But hotel managers reported receiving anxious calls from tour operators in Europe fearing for their clients' safety in view of media reports of the killings.

Tourism is Kenya's biggest source of jobs and hard currency, earning $465 million in 1996. More than half of last year's 770,000 visitors headed for the stunning beaches and lively nightlife of the Mombasa area.
"Tour operators are getting worried in Europe," said Joshua Mwenda, chairman of the Kenya Association of Hotel Keepers and Caterers.
"The image of Kenya is dented, cancellations will be there because people are worried," said Najib Balala, chairman of Mombasa and Coast Tourist Association.
"We are briefing our overseas agents. We are telling them not to panic and at the moment there is a smooth flow of tourist traffic from the airport to the coast."

Hotel managers said their guests were unaffected by the violence in surrounding areas. "They are all happy, they feel secure inside the resort," Devos Jean, deputy manager of the Ocean Village, told Reuters.
"I didn't get any cancellations. The clients are only wondering why there are so many policemen running around."

Ben Ong'uti, resident manager of Diani Reef Hotel, one of the largest hotels on the Kenyan coast, said: "So far we have only had one inquiry on security concerns, but like everyone else we are worried that violence does not spread."

The only tourists directly affected so far were four Swiss and one Malian who fled a guest house torched by raiders in Mtwapa village on Saturday. Others have faced delays of up to an hour on the Mombasa ferry for security checks.

Coast Province Police Chief Francis Gichuki said: "These people are not targetting tourists, but we understand the importance of tourism and are liasing with tour operators to ensure that tourists are not harmed."
Sources at the Serena hotel in Mombasa said the Aga Khan, spiritual leader of Islam's Ismaili community, had cancelled a planned visit.
